title: Extending the Design
description: Extend the parking lot with EV charging stations, payment systems, dynamic pricing, and occupancy optimization.

segments.text: The basic parking lot works. But modern parking systems need EV charging, automated payment, dynamic pricing, and real-time optimization. Let's extend our design to handle all of these.

EV charging spots are a specialization of ParkingSpot. Add a ChargingSpot subclass with chargerType (Level 2, DC Fast), chargingStatus, and powerOutput. An EV vehicle should prefer charging spots but can use regular ones.

A ChargingSession tracks start time, energy consumed in kilowatt-hours, and cost. The charging rate depends on the charger type and the vehicle's maximum intake. Bill separately from parking or bundle them together.
Payment integration requires a PaymentGateway interface. Implementations include CreditCardPayment, MobileWalletPayment, and PrepaidCardPayment. Support partial payments and refunds for early exits.

segments.thought_prompt: A parking lot is 80% full on weekdays but 20% full on weekends. How would you use pricing to balance utilization?

segments.text: Dynamic pricing. Use the Strategy pattern with time-based and occupancy-based pricing strategies. When occupancy exceeds eighty percent, surge pricing kicks in. Weekends get discounted rates. Prices update in real time.

Add a reservation system. Users book spots in advance with a time window. The system must prevent double-booking and handle no-shows with automatic cancellation after a grace period. This is an interval scheduling problem.

Spot assignment optimization: assign vehicles to minimize walking distance from entry. Use a nearest-available algorithm weighted by floor and distance from elevators. The objective function balances utilization and user convenience.

IoT sensors at each spot detect occupancy in real time. Ultrasonic or camera-based sensors publish events to a message queue. The system updates spot status and triggers display board refreshes within seconds.

Analytics layer: track peak hours, average duration, revenue per spot, and EV charging utilization. Store events in a time-series database. Dashboards help operators make decisions about pricing and capacity expansion.

segments.thought_prompt: If you manage a chain of 500 parking lots across a city, how would you architect the central management system?

segments.text: Each lot runs independently with local state. A central service aggregates analytics and manages pricing policies. Event-driven architecture with Kafka handles the cross-lot communication. The extended parking lot teaches you real-world system evolution, adding features without breaking the original design.
